name: Associated Press standards for generative AI in journalism
title: Associated Press standards for generative AI in journalism
answer: This is the Associated Press page setting out its standards for generative AI in journalism. AP says its guiding values are accuracy, fairness and speed, and that AI can serve these values but will not replace journalists. The most useful point is that any generative AI output must be treated as unvetted source material, so AP staff must apply editorial judgment and AP sourcing standards before publication. The page also states AP does not allow generative AI to add or subtract elements in photos, video or audio.

sections.body: The Associated Press publishes this page. It is AP's own standards guidance for using generative artificial intelligence in journalism. It states that AP's news report is guided by accuracy, fairness and speed, and that AP has developed guidance for using generative AI, including how and when it should be used. The text does not give a publication date or named author. Its scope is AP staff and AP's news report, with references to AP's Statement of News Values and Principles.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AP says the central role of the AP journalist, gathering, evaluating and ordering facts into news stories, video, photography and audio, will not change. AP does not see AI as a replacement of journalists. The guidance says any output from a generative AI tool should be treated as unvetted source material. AP staff must apply editorial judgment and AP's sourcing standards when considering any information for publication. AP does not alter any elements of its photos, video or audio, so it does not allow generative AI to add or subtract any elements. AP will refrain from transmitting any AI-generated images that are suspected or proven to be false depictions of reality. If an AI-generated illustration or work of art is the subject of a news story, it may be used as long as it is clearly labeled as such in the caption. AP also encourages journalists to exercise due caution and diligence to ensure material coming into AP from other sources is free of AI-generated content. The text warns that generative AI makes it easier for people to intentionally spread misinformation and disinformation through altered words, photos, video or audio, including content that may have no signs of alteration and appear realistic and authentic. To avoid using such content inadvertently, journalists should exercise the same caution they normally would, including trying to identify the source of the original content, doing a reverse image search to help verify an image's origin, and checking for reports with similar content from trusted media.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numerical figures. It does set out positions. AP says any output from a generative AI tool should be treated as unvetted source material. AP does not allow generative AI to add or subtract any elements in photos, video or audio. AP will refrain from transmitting AI-generated images that are suspected or proven to be false depictions of reality. An AI-generated illustration or work of art may be used if it is the subject of a news story and is clearly labeled in the caption. AP encourages journalists to ensure material from other sources is free of AI-generated content.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Media can use this source to see a major news organization's written rules for generative AI. It is useful because it states what AP permits, what it requires staff to verify, and what it will not publish. It also shows how a newsroom frames AI as a tool that must serve accuracy, fairness and speed rather than replace journalists. The page is a direct policy statement from AP, so it can serve as a reference point when comparing how media organizations set editorial boundaries for AI-generated content.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: The text does not give a publication date, named author, or detailed procedures for enforcement, review or discipline. It does not define generative AI or list specific tools. It is AP's own guidance for AP staff and does not cover other newsrooms, platforms or the wider media industry. It is a policy statement rather than a full operational manual, and it does not address advertising, entertainment or non-news uses. It also does not say how AP will detect AI-generated content beyond the caution and verification steps it describes.
